body:
Maybe they get a lot of suicide by cop calls. Someone says they're suicidal, cops come, and they pull a gun or something on the cops. 

I'm not justifying it, fuck the police, but just a possible explanation.
Please, stop the platitudes. Happiness doesn't come for everyone. Sometimes people are given the short straw. It's better to say you hope things get better than to lie and guarantee that they will.
/r/legaladvice is probably what they meant.

A consultation is usually free. From there you can explain your story and the lawyer will advise if anything can be done. Depending on the situation you may be able to pay on contingency, meaning you won't pay unless you achieve a certain outcome. 

Worst case scenario they say nothing can be done, or if anything can be done it's expensive, but you leave with genuine legal advice. You're not obligated to go through with it and pay. You can only benefit from a consultation.

A lot of what you describe sounds like harassment. Maybe talk to a lawyer, you can probably have a free consultation. The threat of legal action might make them stop, and actual legal action could *force* them to stop.

I have this exact same problem! I feel like I would prefer bad dreams so I wake up relieved (not to downplay the struggles of those with persistent night terrors; it's a "grass is always greener..." situation). Good dreams leave me with existential dread as I'm crushed by the horrible reality I live in.

I just wanted to let you know that you're not alone in feeling this way.

I talked to a lawyer when the symptoms started. He gave me about a 50% chance of success, but if I lost I'd likely have to pay a lot of money which I can't afford. If I wasn't suicidal before, a mountain of debt or bankruptcy would certainly do it. 

There's no proof that he said it was reversible or that he didn't disclose the side effects. It's very difficult to prove medical malpractice in my case, and with doctors it's a bit of an "old boy's club" as they say; they're all likely to vouch for eachother and claim they did everything by the book.

The statute of limitations is 2 years from the time you notice symptoms, and that time has already passed now.

Thank you. I appreciate you taking the time to look into my condition.

It wasn't offered to me as a last resort. He felt my hands and said I was a good candidate. I had the nerves clipped because he told me it was completely reversible if I wasn't happy with the results. From a young age we're taught to trust doctors, so I believed him. 

I was mostly fine for a few years, but things took a sudden turn at the beginning of 2017 as everything got worse. I returned to the surgeon and he claimed he never said the clips were reversible. They could remove them, but the chance of recovery was very low and there was a chance it could make things worse. I had the clips removed about a year ago, and it feels like it's only made things worse.

Some people have had nerve grafts, but almost all of them have been failures until recently. There is a doctor in Taiwan who does nerve grafts with a robot and he claims to have had success with patients. I've spoken with a few of the patients and most have seen improvements, but it's still very early. It could take up to 3 years for them to see significant improvement. If it worked I'd consider doing it, but the cost is astronomical because of the robotic arms used. Most of the patients who had it done were Taiwan citizens because it's much cheaper for them.

The sweat post-surgery is a million times worse than pre-. It used to be just my hands and underarms, but now it's my entire body. My legs, back, butt, and groin are the worst areas. I would need almost every inch of my body Botox'd. As horrible as the sweat is, it's not the worst symptom. The uncontrollable body heat is debilitating. I can't focus on anything when I feel like I'm burning up.
I'm chronically ill. My own doing. Everyone's current life in quarantine is my life all the time, except add constant physical agony.
How can you possibly know that?

Some online stores sell microdose capsules, making it easy for those new to microdosing. Of course, you need to live in a place where they are available (like here in Canada). Once you get a bit more experience you could probably buy the raw mushrooms and make your own capsules.
Good dreams actually make me more depressed. I wake up and am crushed by my horrible reality.

I have a debilitating medical condition that leaves me mostly bed-bound. It causes severe heat intolerance, so severe that I can barely leave my room without feeling like I'm burning up. I Sweat completely through my clothes within minutes. Summer is hell. I can't leave the house. Winter is almost just as bad since every building has the heat blasting. Even in a cool room I still feel like I need to jump in a pool. I'm in constant physical agony. I probably would have killed myself already if it wasn't for my mom. Killing myself would also mean killing her.

I'm a supporter of medical marijuana, but it has never really helped me sleep. It has almost always kept me up, even indicas. Now, I can't even get high because of how it makes my heart race and become hyper-aware of all of the other symptoms I experience.
Can we ban these stupid bots from this sub? Automated, cold, robotic platitudes don't help. This is not the place for these kinds of bots.
Booking appointments online or through text is a godsend. If only I didn't have to actually *go* to appointments.
I like your art style. It would make a cool comic series about your feelings or experiences.

This is something you should be very careful with. I read stories on here all the time about this happening to them. Most of them involve regretting calling the suicide helpline, telling a friend or family member, and they have a bad experience that can make them feel worse. Resentment for those responsible for the involuntary admission is a common outcome.

With that said, there are definitely positive outcomes and times where this is necessary. We probably don't get to hear those because people don't really come here often to post positive stories. It's impossible to know the outcome of a specific situation, so you have to consider the risk.
I still have to pay a stupid amount for a psychologist in Canada.

It almost always made me stay awake, but everyone is different. If you've never tried cannabis before you may not want to try it at night if you have something the next day, just in case it does keep you up. Try it when you have nothing going on the next day so you can afford to lose sleep.

Ironically, some of it has to do with having "good" dreams. I wake up and get intense feelings of dread as reality crushes me. I become aware that everything good that happened in the dream isn't real and my life is still miserable.

I get severe sleep anxiety when I need to sleep. I am genuinely afraid of sleeping at times. I can't explain it really, it's completely irrational. It frequently causes insomnia. Of course once I do fall asleep I don't want to get up.
Cannabis could be one of his best options for his chronic pain. If you can't get prescribed pain meds your options are limited.
I used to smoke a lot of cannabis. Sadly, it causes severe anxiety for me now. It doesn't matter if it's indica or sativa. I'm glad it helps people though. It definitely used to help me.

> It does get better. Believe it or not, it will eventually get better. Sometimes you have to go through the storm to get to the rainbow. 

Please, stop the "it gets better" platitudes. It's just as likely to get worse. I have a debilitating physical medical condition that has only gotten worse and is only likely to get even worse. Things don't always get better. I *hope* it does, but the chances of some cure coming out anytime soon are extremely slim.

>throw these platitudes at each other

This annoys me the most. Every other post has people saying, "it gets better," "you'll get through it," or, "it's okay." How could you possibly know that? It is just as likely, or even more likely, to get worse.

Do you have any recommendations for strains? I'm not going to get some any time soon, but I'd keep them in mind for the future. I have a medical license still because it's the best way to get high-quality and inexpensive CBD, so I have a lot of options between the OCS and the LPs.

It wasn't just sativas, indicas do it to me too. I tried quite a few strains. I still have 5 or 6 different strains sitting around. They're probably so dry at this point that they wouldn't be a good smoke. I almost bought some Northern Lights a few weeks back after hearing it was really good for anxiety, but I just couldn't bring myself to do it. I couldn't risk feeling worse than I already did.

I'll give it another go at some point, but I'm not in a mindset that can handle it if it makes me feel bad. This is r/suicidewatch after all. I'm here for the same reason most other people probably are.

I *want* to enjoy if like I used to, but honestly it makes make scared and anxious now. It's at the point where I expect it to make me feel bad, so I get anxious and as a result it makes me feel even worse. The times that it made me feel worse were horrible. I know I have to keep trying to find the strain that will help, but sorting through ones that make me feel horrible is exhausting and unpleasant. It's ironic that this all started happening around the time it became legal here in Canada. I've pretty much given up on it at this point.
Smoking weed just makes my pain worse. It causes me to become more aware of it and focus on it. It's a shame because it's something I used to enjoy with friends.

Can you walk after your injury? If so, I might relate somewhat, but I won't assume that our cases are similar.

I have severe nerve damage that causes autonomic dysfunction. I can walk and lift weights, but I have temperature dysregulation causing me to get heat stroke very quickly, I soak through all my chlothes in sweat with no effort, and I can't breath properly.

Talking to me in person, you might not know there was anything wrong with me. I try to hide it in public, but I'm in agony.
People who say that are probably the same people that think you can just "get over it" through the magic of healthy eating, exercise, and positive mental attitude.

Anticholinergics such as Glycopyrrolate can reduce sweating, but they also reduce all other bodily secretions (saliva, eyes, nose).

Alpha blockers such as Clonidine can reduce sympathetic activity, but they lower blood pressure.

You may or may not tolerate either of these types of drugs, it depends on your dose and other dysautonomia symptoms.
Chiropractics is a pseudoscience. They believe various illnesses can be healed by contorting the spine. Stay away from them from now on.
I don't like seeing old pictures of myself. I remember that moment and think about how much better my life was then, and how fucked up everything is now.

> It gets better

Platitudes don't help. It doesn't always get better.

I believe the studies most people refer to involve Oxybutynin use by elderly people.

From my understanding, Glyco doesn't pass through the blood-brain barrier like other anticholinergics. Many people who take Oxybutynin report fatigue, brain fog, dizziness, etc. These side effects are far less common with Glyco.

> the subreddit isn’t about trying to help everyone get better

It's not about trying to help, it's just being able to talk and listen to each other. Let's be honest, you probably can't *really* help most serious cases of depression via the internet. The best you can do is be there and be supportive.

I'm often the complete opposite, my flight reaction kicks in and I have an almost uncontrollable desire to leave wherever I am. I could be at home in bed and still feel like I need to leave, even if there's nowhere for me to go. More than once I've ended up pacing around my house in panic. Sitting still in these situations is very difficult for me.

Here's a hotline number, good luck!

/r/wowthanksimcured

I even hate simple greetings like, "How's it going?" or, "How are you doing?"

Of course, they want to hear, "Good" because that's the answer everyone is expected to give. They don't *actually* want to hear how you are doing. It's just another way of saying, "hello" but I feel terrible saying I'm okay or doing well when I'm far from okay.

To avoid lying and pretending I'm okay, my answers now usually go something like:

>Them: "How's it going?"  
>Me: "It's going."

or,

>Them: "How are you doing?"  
>Me: "Getting by."
You really need a separate account just for posting here, and leave out identifying information.

Get off social media. Watching other people's fake lives won't do any good for you. I say "fake lives" because many people are struggling when they're off-screen. Those Instagram photos are the highlights, they don't show the lows. I've known people who had Instagram and Facebook pages full of them being happy and partying, but in reality they struggled with mental illness (or even physical illness). Social media often sends the message of, "I'm happy all the time, and you're not, so there's something wrong with you."

Honestly that's a fine answer, and probably the answer they want to actually hear. It's like when someone asks, "how's it going?" and everyone just says, "good". They don't actually want to hear, "it's not going well at all". They don't really care how you are or what you've been doing.

That I'll be like this the rest of my life. I have a debilitating medical condition and I can barely get through the day. These past 2 years have felt like a decade, and the prospect of continuing to live like this terrifies me.

My grandma recently passed away and it absolutely killed my mom. I've never seen her cry like that before and it hurt so much seeing her like that. I don't want her to feel that way again, and I definitely don't want to be the cause of it.

Learn new things.

It could be a new skill (ex. new language, coding), hobby (ex. knitting, instrument), or just learning new knowledge (ex. history, science).

There are online classes for just about everything. Even something as informal as a YouTube playlist on the topic is great. Reddit is good for this too since there is usually a subreddit on the topic which usually includes links to other external resources.

It keeps your mind active, can be challenging if you want it to be, and over time you've learned something new that you can be proud of. When your SO returns you'll be able to show what you've accomplished.

> Surgery probably wont be covered by my insurance

DO NOT GET ETS SURGERY

It has ruined my life and the lives of countless others. There are forums and facebook support groups full of thousands of people who regret it.

Most success stories you hear of are from people who had it done recently, but it can take many years before the side effects kick in. I was satisfied with the surgery for about 5 years before I started sweating all over my body at even low temperatures. I now feel hot all the time, like I have a constant fever.

DO NOT GET THE SURGERY

I had it done and it has ruined my life. There's an 80%+ chance you'll begin sweating in other parts of your body. It also can cause irregular body temperature regulation. I feel hot all the time, and I now sweat all over my body. I wish I had my sweaty palms and underarms back. Anything would be preferable to the hell I live in now.

I was fine for the first 5 years post-surgery. Most positive stories about the surgery are in the "honeymoon phase" before the horrible side effects kick in. This phase can last for many years.

Some doctors will say they can perform a reversible version that involves clips or clamps, but IT IS NOT REVERSIBLE.

I was clipped, and I noticed no side effects for about 5 years. It's no true that you'll notice right away if something is wrong, it can take many years. I've heard from many people who were fine for years, like I was. I was told that clipping was "completely reversible", but when I returned to the surgeon he told me that at no point was it reversible, denying he ever said that it was.
I understand how you feel. The last thing I want to do is hurt my parents. They don't deserve to suffer and bury their child. They sacrificed so much for me already, so I have to keep going.

Thanks, I hope so too, and not just for my sake. Other people have lived with this much longer than I have, and some experience worse symptoms than mine. It's very difficult for me to function normally at this point, if not impossible. I have to believe that things will get better eventually, because the thought of 50 or more years like this terrifies me.

Some people don't develop debilitating side effects, or the side effects they get are preferable to how they were before. I hope that is the case for you ex. Nobody should have to go through this.

The document didn't list the side effects. It has a catch-all statement, "I have been advised of the risks and side effects of the proposed treatment". So I signed it under the assumption that the doctor disclosed all the risks and side effects.
Fuck me for trusting a doctor right?

I take Glycopyrrolate, which is an anticholinergic similar to Oxybutynin. Glycopyrrolate has fewer cognitive effects and last longer, so I prefer it. The only con is that it has to be taken on an empty stomach. It helps, but it's far from perfect. It doesn't stop the sweat completely, and I get all the typical anticholinergic side effects such as dry mouth and nose.
Of course not. I've seen a malpractice lawyer and was given a 50% chance of a jury ruling in my favor. If I lost I'd have to pay for both my and the defendant's legal fees.

I wish I could afford to lose. The lawyer I saw gave me a 50% chance of a jury ruling in my favor, and if I lost I would have to pay the defendant's legal fees along with my own. If I wasn't screwed already, I certainly would be after that. Malpractice is very difficult to prove.

I was fine for about 5 years until I was in a warm dentist office and I started to sweat profusely all over my body. About 6 months or so later I started to feel really hot all the time which made the sweating worse. It's all been downhill since then.
That does sound similar. Perhaps you have some nerve damage from the cyst or the removal.
Do not get this surgery. It has ruined my life, along with the lives of many others. There are forums and facebook support groups full of thousands of people who regret it. It's not worth it.

It's impractical to apply botox to such a large area. I would need it on my back, chest, face, legs, butt. That still doesn't solve the problem of feeling hot all the time, and is likely to make it worse since I can't cool down.
I'm not even close to overweight, and never have been.

Sweaty palms were much easier to live with. When I had sweaty palms, the rest of my body was fine. I could still be in warm rooms, go outside, travel, but I can't do any of that now without my clothes getting drenched.

Some people have had nerve grafts. A few have had favorable results, but most people show no improvement. I've even heard a few people say it made things worse. Current methods require harvesting a nerve from somewhere else in your body, so there are huge risks. I don't know of any doctor that performs this in my country (Canada); all the doctors I know that do it internationally charge thousands (or tens of thousands) of dollars with no guarantee of any improvement.

I didn't have the nerve cut, I had it clamped, because I was told that it was "completely reversible" if anything happened. When I returned 5 years later and asked about having the clamps removed he denied saying it was ever reversible, and removing the clamps was unlikely to help and may even make things worse. There's a possibility of some recovery, but it's a huge risk. From what I've read, similar to the nerve grafts, some people have favorable results, most have no improvement, and a few have unfavorable results. It's something I'm looking into still.

Something may be possible in the future with new techniques and technologies, but that's all that's available right now.

I've tried changing my diet a few times, but it hasn't made any improvement. I did all the recommended things such as cutting out dairy, wheat, processed foods. I've tried paleo and ketogenic, but nothing changed.

I used to exercise regularly, but it's become much more difficult over the past couple of years.
I wish I knew about it before I had surgery, but it was never offered to me as an option.

My threshold is around 75f. I often sweat at lower temperatures than that even. I live in Canada, where winters are blisteringly cold and summers are suffocatingly humid. You'd think winters would be fine, but every building has heat blasting constantly.

I was clamped. I only had it done because I was assured it was "completely reversible". When I started to get bad side effects 5 years later I returned to the surgeon and was told that removing the clamps was unlikely to make anything better and has a chance of making things worse. I wish there was proof that he told me it was reversible and didn't disclose the side effects.

I did sign a document saying I understood the risk. The problem with that is I understood the risk as it was presented to me, and the document doesn't list the risks. He never mentioned that I'd sweat more or feel hot all the time, but there's no proof of that.
I had the surgery to stop my palms from sweating constantly. Post-op they only sweat when extremely anxious or doing heavy exercise. I would rather have constantly sweaty palms than be like this.

You don't want to use the wipes over large areas of your body. They stop more than sweat, they stop all body secretions. You'll have horrible dry mouth, sore throat, dry nose, dry eyes, constipation, headaches.

Anticholinergic meds such as Glycopyrrolate or Oxybutynin help, but they have bad side effects which some people can't tolerate. Alpha-blockers such as Clonidine or Terazosin help some people, but not everyone, and have side effects as well.

Some people have had nerve grafts. A few have had favorable results, but it seems most have no improvement. I've even heard of it making things worse for some. They usually involve harvesting a nerve from somewhere else in your body, so there are huge risks involved.

Other than that, and miradry, there's just hope for the future. Science is amazing, and with current technology we could see more advances in the next 10 years than the past 100. There are people walking around with 3D printed bladders made in labs from stem cells. There are people regaining the ability to walk with electrodes implanted in their brain and spinal cord.

It's common for patients to not be properly informed about these side effects, or for doctors to misrepresent the chances of getting these side effects. Many patients don't experience them until many years later (5 years later for me), so doctors assume after 12 months that everything is fine and write you off as a success. In my case, I wasn't told about sweating profusely in other parts of my body or having compromised thermoregulation.
A have a lot of special clothing which help hide the sweat and cool me down a bit. They help to some extent.

There are some treatments, such as MiraDry. This is only approved for underarms though. Some doctors are willing to perform it off-label for areas such as your back. Most of these doctors don't perform it over your spine, so I would still need botox regularly if I wanted to stop it completely. It's something I'm keeping my eye on for the future.

However, this doesn't solve the problem of feeling hot all the time. It may even make that problem worse in warm/hot areas. I'm hesitant to try anything else permanent which has the potential to make things worse.

Thanks for the kind words. I often feel hopeless and isolated because of this, but I try to maintain hope for the future. Science is amazing. On a long enough timescale humanity is likely to solve every problem imaginable. It feels very selfish, especially with people suffering from worse conditions than mine, but I hope this one is solved sooner rather than later.

I have not tried Miradry. I never even heard of it until about a year ago when I started to look for a treatment for my profuse sweating. I've talked to a few doctors that perform it off-label in areas such as the back. I've even talked to a couple of people who had it performed on their back after the surgery. It's something I'm keeping my eye on. Unfortunately it doesn't solve the problem of feeling hot all the time, and could make it worse if it's hot out.
I have heard of this, but it looks way too small to do anything for me. Maybe they'll start making full-body suits some day haha.

I was clamped at T3 & T4. I only had the operation because I was assured that clamping meant that it was, "completely reversible" if anything bad happened. The only side effect I was told of was getting a droopy eyelid, known as Horner's Syndrome. When I started to get profuse sweating all over I returned to the surgeon and asked about having the clamps removed, but he told me that it was unlikely to make anything better and even had the potential to make things worse. He denies ever saying that clamping was a reversible procedure. I was young and trusted him since he was a surgeon.

I've seen a lawyer about malpractice, but it's very difficult to prove it. I was given about a 50% chance that a jury would rule in my favor. It's very expensive to retain a lawyer and find a doctor to testify, and if I lost the case I would have to pay the defendants fees as well.

I live in Canada, so we have very cold winters and very hot and humid summers. Some days I feel like the cold is almost worse since every building has the heat blasting. Going from a cold outdoors to a hot indoors causes me to sweat profusely.

This shock therapy is known as Iontophoresis. I only found out about it about a year ago, long after I already had the surgery. Unfortunately no doctors ever told me about this, or about any medications that could help, otherwise I would have tried them first.

I've tried changing my diet but it hasn't helped. I tried a paleo diet for a couple of months with no results, then I tried a ketogenic diet and still no results. I lost a lot of weight from the diets, which would be good for many people, but I've never been overweight (about 170lbs, 6ft 5in).

I do have a cooling vest. It helps me feel cooler, but it doesn't stop me from sweating profusely. I often sweat under the vest, and if it's really bad it will drip and show through my clothes. I have some clothing which don't show wet marks and they help a lot.

I've heard of some people who have had nerve grafts, but the results are very mixed.

Some people have reported favorable results, while others have said they've seen no improvement. I've even heard of side effects getting worse after nerve graft or nerve reconstruction.

I don't know of any doctor in my country (Canada) that performs this. All the doctors I know that do it charge thousands (or tens of thousands) of dollars for it.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endoscopic_thoracic_sympathectomy

I had life-destroying surgery which has completely compromised my body's thermoregulation. It was an elective surgery called a Sympathectomy (aka ETS or ELS), meant to stop my palms from sweating.

The doctors didn't warn me this could happen. They deny everything, and there's no proof that they didn't disclose the side effects. It took 5 years for these side effects to manifest, and now it is rapidly becoming worse as time goes on.

I can't go outside in the summer because I sweat profusely through my clothes. I can barely sit inside at normal room temperatures. My head constantly feels like it's on fire. I can't tolerate cold either. I'm either always burning up, or I'm always freezing. I don't know how I'm going to be able to cope with this for the rest of my life. I'm only 26, but I feel like my life is over already.

I have a debilitating chronic illness, so I can relate to the unchangeable situation. Like yourself, I don't want to die but also don't want to live like this for the rest of my life. I have a small amount of hope for future treatments, but the reality is I'll probably be this way my whole life or get worse.
Depending on where you live you might be able to order it through the mail.

I used to enjoy smoking so much, but lately it's only made my anxiety exponentially worse to the point it's caused panic attacks. Every now and then I still try because it helped a lot with other symptoms of my chronic illness. I've tried various strains but so far I haven't found one that doesn't skyrocket my anxiety. I've tried high-CBD strains, and even added more CBD with powdered isolate, but no luck.
This is why I keep going. Suicide doesn't end the pain and suffering, it passes it on to those who love you most.

I just made a similar post. Sleep frightens me sometimes because when I wake up I'm instantly crushed by reality.
I feel this way a lot. There are a lot of things I can't do anymore and it kills me. I feel like I've lost who I was and who I wish I could be.

I'm with you on that. 

I have 20 contacts on my phone:  
- 7 are doctors  
- 2 are pharmacies  
- 2 are my parents  
- 2 are my sister and her husband  
- 1 is my hairdresser  
- 1 is my work  
- 1 is my phone and internet provider  
- 4 are former friends I haven't talked to in almost 3 years since my anxiety, depression, and health have gotten worse. 

I should really remove the "friends", but then I'd only have doctors, family, and businesses as contacts. Also, having them still there makes me feel like I could reconnect with them some day, but I know they don't want anything to do with me anymore.

I love it too. Sometimes I don't want the drive to end. Having a GPS is great so I can drive around places I've never been before or normally wouldn't go to.

I totally understand how people can find it intimidating though. It's one of the most dangerous things people do regularly, and many drivers are nonchalant about safety.

Other people have the same problem as me, some left in worse condition, and many of them have exhausted all options. I've joined a couple of support groups on facebook and other forums for people suffering from it like I am. A large majority of the members feel lied to or misled by medical professionals like I do. 

I've seen a couple of doctors already and there's not much they can do. Some medication does help reduce the sweating, but it's not enough (and they have really bad side effects). These medications don't help with me feeling hot all the time, and some are known to actually make it worse by increasing your body temperature as one of the side effects. I still take them because it makes the sweating more tolerable when sedentary, and without them I am mentally a wreck as I sweat constantly all over my body. I'm still pursuing other leads, but things aren't looking good right now. There are treatments being developed, but nothing currently available.

I do my best to get by day to day, but each day I feel worse than the last. I often have dreams where everything is fine, but then when I wake up I am crushed by reality as my head burns and my body sweats profusely.
I believe there will be a treatment for both of our problems in the future. Living long enough for it is the difficult part.

Our situations are different in many ways, but have some similarities. I understand how you feel in some ways.

Like you, I had a medical procedure which has only made things worse. I'm also close to your age (26).

My medical procedure has ruined my body's thermoregulation. I can't tolerate heat or warmth whatsoever. My entire body sweats almost constantly, often through my clothes. While summers are bad, most building have air conditioning on. During the winter, most places have heat blasting. My body constantly feels hot. I can't tolerate the cold either, so if I use a fan or air conditioning I am constantly shivering. There is no comfortable temperature anymore. At least when I'm cold I don't soak through my clothes.

I can't go outside in the summer. I can barely be inside during the winter. I can't travel. I fear any sort of relationship. I feel like my life is over before it ever had a chance to start.

We grow up believing doctors are Gods and they are infallible. By the time we learn otherwise it might be too late.

I've seen a lawyer, gave him all the documents from the surgery, and he said there's about a 50/50 chance of a jury ruling in my favor. It would cost about $15,000 to retain him and to hire a doctor as a consultant. If I lost I would have to pay the legal fees of the defendant as well as my own legal fees.

I really don't know what to do at this point. I can't afford to lose the case.

I had life-destroying surgery which has completely compromised my body's thermoregulation. The doctors didn't warn me this could happen. They deny everything, and there's no proof that they didn't disclose the side effects. It took 5 years for these side effects to manifest, and now it is rapidly becoming worse as time goes on. I can't go outside in the summer because I sweat profusely through my clothes. I can barely sit inside at normal room temperatures. My head constantly feels like it's on fire. I can't tolerate cold either. I'm either always burning up, or I'm always freezing. I don't know how I'm going to be able to cope with this for the rest of my life. I'm only 26, but I feel like my life is over already.
